03.r: Greek often puts the article before a personal name; English does not.

04.r: Moves from the coin to Jesus' answer.
04.n: The KJV's opening 'And' answers to a different word in its Greek text; see the note on the Textus Receptus.

08.r: The neuter plural article: whatever belongs to Caesar.
08.n: Mark puts 'the things of Caesar' first, ahead of the verb, which gives the phrase weight; this study keeps that order. The Greek has no noun: 'the things' stands for the neuter plural article.

09.r: Caesar as owner of what is to be rendered to him.

10.r: Give back what is owed, as a debt is paid.
10.n: The question had been about 'giving' tribute; Jesus answers with ἀποδίδωμι, 'give back'. Abbott-Smith notes its special use of wages, debts and oaths: to render what is due, to pay. Following the register for an obligation, this study renders it 'render'; the YLT's 'Give back' brings out the 'back'.

11.r: The one to whom the debt is due.

12.r: Joins the second half of the ruling.

14.r: The article with 'God'; English does not use it.

15.r: God as owner of what is to be rendered to him.

16.r: The article with 'God'; English does not use it.

17.r: The one to whom the second debt is due.
17.n: The verb 'render' is not repeated; it carries over from the first half.

19.r: Imperfect tense: their astonishment went on.
19.n: Abbott-Smith calls this a strengthened form of the usual verb for wondering, 'to wonder greatly', and lists this verse as its only New Testament use. Of the six translations only the ASV, 'marvelled greatly', shows the strengthening.

20.r: Marks the cause of their wonder.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus opens with καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς, 'and answering', where our text has δέ, which is why the KJV reads 'And Jesus answering said'. It reads ἐθαύμασαν, 'they marvelled', for the stronger ἐξεθαύμαζον, 'they were marvelling greatly'. It also has ἀπόδοτε, 'render', at another place in the sentence.
